attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production raster sprite source for HARVEST THE NIGHT, a cozy farm that becomes a fortress against zombies at night.
Primary request: terrain/edge_n, one narrow NORTH-facing grass-to-soil/path transition overlay. This is a new isolated tile overlay.
Input images: Image 1 accepted grass material reference; Image 2 approved neutral-day world style reference. These are references, not edit targets.
Style/medium: hand-crafted pixel art with deliberate joined pixel clusters, colored material planes, restrained texture and clean forms.
Composition/framing: orthographic top-down rectangular tile, full square source canvas corresponding to final 16x16 pixels, pivot 8,16. No perspective block.
Lighting/mood: neutral warm daytime material. Flat top-view grass with no directional specular shading; this edge will be rotated clockwise for east/south/west, so no cast shadows.
Color palette: accepted grass green #6a9646 with extremely sparse #4e7a35 grass tuft tips. The top boundary and left/right endpoints are flat #6a9646.
Scene/backdrop: TRUE TRANSPARENT outside a narrow grass band touching the TOP of the canvas.
Constraints: no labels, text, watermark, UI, scenery, ground shadow, objects or underlying soil/path.
Avoid: smooth painting, blur, gradients, noisy grass blades, flowers, thick outlines, diamond isometric tiles and tiny details.

WATER/TRANSITION brief: Produce ONE named grass fringe edge, NORTH N=1; runtime rotates the same accepted flat material for E=2/S=4/W=8 and composites all 16 cardinal masks. Warm farm earth is the underlying separate material, not baked here. True transparency outside the overlay; no shore sliding or swimming pixels.

Exact native contract: The full top TWO pixel rows, about 12.5% of the square height, are an uninterrupted narrow band of flat #6a9646 grass running edge-to-edge. Two or three small joined tufts protrude down by only ONE extra native pixel near the CENTER half of this band; no disconnected speckles. Left/right end quarters have exactly the same two-pixel thickness, no tufts there, so neighboring segments connect. Everything below the 3-pixel depth (81.25% of canvas) is genuinely transparent. The overlay canvas must remain square with most of it empty; do not zoom the band or center it vertically. No dirt backing, no bottom border, no white/checkerboard drawn into the image.
attempts.decision: Accepted after measured source alpha, native/3x masks and caps, repeated water patches, all 50 actual day/dusk/night captures and two real-render water loops; source-owned geometry and static contacts pass.

attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production raster sprite source for HARVEST THE NIGHT, a cozy farm that becomes a fortress against zombies at night.
Primary request: terrain/shore_n, ONE static north-facing shoreline overlay, at the TOP of an otherwise transparent square tile. New isolated overlay.
Input images: Image 1 accepted narrow grass-edge source for matching green/band scale; Image 2 approved neutral-day style reference for warm earth against cool water; Image 3 accepted grass material for boundary green. References only, no edit target.
Style/medium: coherent hand-crafted pixel art with deliberate joined pixel clusters, restrained texture, readable material planes and clean forms.
Composition/framing: flat top-down material on a rectangular grid. Full square source corresponds to 16x16 native pixels, pivot 8,16; generated source must survive reduction.
Lighting/mood: neutral daytime material, no cast ground shadow. Flat material planes without directional specular lighting; source will rotate clockwise for the other three cardinal directions.
Color palette: grass #6a9646; warm earth #96704a and #7a5838; darker wet earth #5c422a; restrained water contact #2b5480. No white foam, luminous cyan or outlines.
Scene/backdrop: genuine transparent canvas outside the narrow TOP bank; no water painted under it.
Constraints: no labels, text, watermark, UI, object, dock, islands, perspective block or scenery.
Avoid: smooth painting, blur, gradients, random one-pixel speckles, stones, flowers, detached pixels and thick black borders.

WATER brief: Produce one named bank edge, NORTH N=1. Banks use warm earth, short grass fringe and coherent water contact; bank overlay has true transparency outside the edge. Side maps will be rotated for E=2/S=4/W=8 and composited for all 16 cardinal masks. No shore sliding between water frames, foam noise, diagonal island perspective or baked jetty.

Exact native contract: keep the bank attached to the TOP, edge-to-edge. It occupies only the TOP THREE to FOUR final native pixel rows (about 19-25% of square height): one thin flat green row at the very top, one or two rows of warm brown earth, then a thin subdued dark wet-earth/water contact rim. The bottom contact may step by ONE pixel in the central half, with calm broad shapes. NO isolated grass tips, foam speckles or protruding rocks. The left and right endpoint quarters have exactly identical layer heights and colors, so adjacent bank tiles join perfectly. The remaining 75% of the square canvas is genuinely transparent. Do not enlarge the band to fill the canvas or center it vertically. Bank colors and alpha stay STATIC through the water animation.
attempts.decision: rejected: one native left/right endpoint color mismatch produces a repeated bank seam

attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent raster terrain corner overlay for HARVEST THE NIGHT.
Primary request: ONE north-west rounded earth-bank CORNER cap, terrain/shore_corner_nw, for a pixel-art farm pond.
Input images: Image 1 accepted north shoreline master, a material/color reference only. Create a new corner source; it is not a full straight edge.
Style/medium: hand-crafted top-down pixel-art material with clean joined clusters and restrained texture.
Composition/framing: complete square transparent canvas, final native16x16 with pivot8,16. A very small quarter-circle bank cap touches the TOP LEFT corner. Most of the canvas stays empty.
Lighting/mood: neutral daytime flat material, no cast shadow, no specular lighting, no gradient. Runtime handles dusk/night.
Color palette: corner's green core #46804a, warm earth rim #a87c4e, optional subdued dark wet-earth edge #5c422a; match accepted bank endpoint. No white foam or luminous cyan.
Scene/backdrop: genuine transparency everywhere outside the tiny cap.
Constraints: no scenery, text, watermark, labels, UI, perspective block, jetty, water backing, stones, detached pixels or full border.
Avoid: smooth painting, blur, noise, flowers, zooming the cap, filling the canvas or creating full straight shoreline strips.

WATER brief: one named stationary bank corner NORTH-WEST. Warm earth, short grass core, coherent water contact. True transparent outside the corner. No shore sliding or swimming bank pixels.

Exact contract: the small cap occupies about 12.5% of the full square width and height, just TWO final native pixels. Its geometry is a quarter-circle anchored at the very TOP LEFT: one green core at the corner, warm brown extending only a little to the right and below, ending rounded toward the transparent bottom-right. The incoming edge profiles along TOP and LEFT must be identical: first native pixel green, next native pixel warm brown, then transparency for all remaining14 pixels. Do NOT make an L across the full edges. Keep the rest of the16x16 square transparent and empty. It will be rotated clockwise for NE/SE/SW. This cap joins two accepted straight bank segments meeting a diagonal land tile.
attempts.decision: rejected: native cap endpoint colors differ from accepted bank, and horizontal/vertical browns differ

attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: transparent pixel-art pond bank corner overlay.
Input images: Image 1 EDIT TARGET, tiny north-west bank cap; Image 2 accepted straight bank material/color reference.
Primary request: correct ONLY the material colors of the little cap. Preserve its existing location, shape, size, and full transparent square canvas.
Failure at native16x16: the cap's green maps to #557652 rather than the straight bank's #46804a; its left-side earth maps to #7a5838 rather than the required #a87c4e on BOTH sides.
Correction: use absolutely flat uniform #46804a GREEN in the little top-left core. Use absolutely flat uniform #a87c4e warm BROWN everywhere in the cap's surrounding earth, both its top/right and left/bottom limbs, with no darker brown planes or directional shading. Those two flat colors and true transparency are sufficient. No gradient, texture, shadows, lighting variation, dark outline or blue contact in this tiny cap.
Preserve the exact existing small quarter-circle geometry near the top-left, the existing transparent space, image dimensions and neutral top-down camera. Do NOT enlarge or reposition the cap, add full side strips, scene, labels, glow, objects or detached pixels. It will be cropped/measured and rotated into the other three orientations; opposite incoming profiles must have exactly the same two colors.
attempts.decision: Accepted after measured source alpha, native/3x masks and caps, repeated water patches, all 50 actual day/dusk/night captures and two real-render water loops; source-owned geometry and static contacts pass.

attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: production raster north-bank overlay for HARVEST THE NIGHT.
Input images: Image 1 EDIT TARGET, rejected north-bank candidate; Image 2 accepted grass color/material reference only.
Primary request: correct ONLY the nonmatching left/right endpoint profile of this static narrow north-bank overlay.
Failure measured after nearest reduction to 16x16 and project palette: the left and right bank endpoints differ in one native color, leaving a repeated join seam.
Correction: make the leftmost and rightmost QUARTER of the canvas identical, calm horizontal layer bands with precisely the same thickness and colors: top grass #6a9646, next warm earth #96704a/#7a5838, bottom restrained contact #2b5480. No dots, tufts, varying depth or texture in either end quarter. Continue each layer flat to both outer boundaries. Keep the center's existing shallow shoreline character, but join it continuously to those calm end bands.
Preserve the original full square canvas and narrow band at the very TOP, its total depth about three native pixels, camera, muted palette, genuine transparency below the edge, and flat top-down material. Do not center/enlarge the band, add scenery, water below it, labels, foam, glow, shadow, white/checkerboard pixels or detached speckles. No changes to bank placement or animation; it stays static. This edge will rotate into all four cardinal orientations and must connect without gaps. Native target remains 16x16, pivot 8,16.
attempts.decision: Accepted after measured source alpha, native/3x masks and caps, repeated water patches, all 50 actual day/dusk/night captures and two real-render water loops; source-owned geometry and static contacts pass.

attempts.prompt_text:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production raster sprite source for HARVEST THE NIGHT, a cozy farm that becomes a fortress against zombies at night.
Primary request: terrain/water, terrain/water_b, terrain/water_c: exactly one three-frame subtle water loop.
Input images: Image 1 approved neutral-day style reference; Image 2 accepted quiet grass source for relative contrast only. Neither is an edit target. Create new water art.
Style/medium: coherent hand-crafted pixel art with deliberate pixel clusters, colored outlines, restrained texture, readable material planes and clean forms.
Composition/framing: orthographic three-quarter top-down view on a rectangular grid. Each final native canvas is 16x16 pixels with contact pivot 8,16; this is a downstream import target, so the generated source must remain simple enough to survive reduction.
Lighting/mood: neutral warm daytime, runtime supplies dusk/night lighting. Water is flat top-view material rather than a perspective block.
Color palette: base cool muted blue #3a6ea5, ripple #5a8cc0, sparse shadow #2b5480. Avoid teal, green, white and fluorescent colors. Match the water's calm relative contrast to the accepted grass.
Scene/backdrop: fully opaque edge-to-edge water in ALL three cells; no transparent gutters.
Constraints: no labels, text, watermark, UI, scenery, shoreline, islands, borders, grid lines or baked jetty.
Avoid: smooth painting, vector look, 3D render, anti-aliased halos, blur, gradients, random pixel speckle, thick black boxes, diamond isometric tiles, new gameplay objects, tiny details that disappear at native size.

WATER brief: Produce one three-frame water loop. Water is cool blue with restrained bright horizontal ripple clusters, fully opaque within water tiles; subtle slow motion. Opposite borders match within and across all frames. No shore sliding between frames, foam noise, diagonal island perspective or baked jetty.

STRIP contract: exactly THREE equal SQUARE cells in ONE horizontal strip, ordered initial ripple, ripple shifted slightly RIGHT, ripple softly receding to initial position. Same blue base everywhere. Edge-to-edge cells with no gutter, labels or separator. Keep broad calm areas: at least 94% flat blue base in each cell. Only TWO short low-contrast joined horizontal ripple clusters per cell, each about 2-3 final native pixels long and one pixel thick, well inside the central area. Place one around upper-left interior and one around lower-right interior. Ripples move at most ONE native pixel, no vertical movement. All four outer borders of every cell are completely uniform base blue, with a calm margin at least TWO native pixels wide, so every water frame tiles perfectly with every other. No per-frame size/color drift. This is a material loop source, not a collage of different designs.
attempts.decision: Accepted after measured source alpha, native/3x masks and caps, repeated water patches, all 50 actual day/dusk/night captures and two real-render water loops; source-owned geometry and static contacts pass.
